title: NBA disburses around Rs. 3.79 crore under Access and Benefit Sharing mechanism to 33 States/UTs and National Institutes
body_text:
The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed close to Rs. 3.79 crore as Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) to 33 State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs), the ICAR-National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (NBPGR) and through the Haryana State Biodiversity Board to the Hisar Bovine Sperm Station and Research Centre.
The release covers a diverse range of India's agrobiodiversity, including tomato, chilli, brinjal, cauliflower, watermelon, bitter gourd, bottle gourd, okra, mustard seed varieties and deep-frozen Sahiwal cattle semen. The ABS amount was realised from companies including M/s Bayer Science and Innovation Pvt. Ltd., M/s HM Clause India Pvt. Ltd. and M/s Advanta Enterprises Limited for accessing vegetable and oilseed genetic resources for research and commercial utilisation.
In addition, an ABS amount arose from the Department of Animal Production and Health, Government of Sri Lanka, for access to Sahiwal cattle semen. India's ABS framework, implemented under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 and aligned with the Nagoya Protocol, ensures equitable benefit sharing when biological resources are accessed by users from other countries. As companies had accessed biological resources through markets, traders or intermediaries, the original source of access could not be identified. In such cases, the NBA adopted the benefit-sharing modalities prepared by an Expert Committee and approved by the Authority.
The ABS amount was disbursed proportionately among the SBBs and UTBCs of the States and Union Territories where the respective crops are cultivated, using cultivation-area data published by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. The details of biological resources and ABS amount released to beneficiaries are given below:
Biological Resource Company ABS Amount released States / Beneficiary Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea var. botrytis) seed varieties & hybrids Bayer Science and Innovation Pvt. Ltd. & HM Clause India Pvt. Ltd. Rs 26.98 lakh 30 SBBs/UTBCs Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) seed varieties & hybrids Bayer Science and Innovation Pvt. Ltd. & HM Clause India Pvt. Ltd. Rs 24.32 lakh 25 SBBs/UTBCs Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) seed varieties & hybrids Bayer Science and Innovation Pvt. Ltd. & HM Clause India Pvt. Ltd. Rs 86.56 lakh 31 SBBs/UTBCs Chilli (Capsicum annuum) seed varieties & hybrids Bayer Science and Innovation Pvt. Ltd. & HM Clause India Pvt. Ltd. Rs 83.76 lakh 32 SBBs/UTBCs Brinjal (Solanum melongena) seed varieties & hybrids Bayer Science and Innovation Pvt. Ltd. & HM Clause India Pvt. Ltd. Rs 7.18 lakh 31 SBBs/UTBCs Bitter gourd, Bottle gourd, Brinjal, Cauliflower, Hot pepper, Okra and Tomato germplasm Advanta Enterprises Limited Rs 148 lakh 31 SBBs/UTBCs Mustard (Brassica juncea) seed varieties Advanta Enterprises Limited Rs 0.57 lakh ICAR-NBPGR, New Delhi Sahiwal cattle (Bos indicus) semen Dept. of Animal Production & Health, Sri Lanka Rs 0.98 lakh Hisar Bovine Sperm Station & Research Centre (through Haryana SBB)
The largest share of the ABS amount was released to the following States, reflecting their significant contribution to the cultivation of the respective crops:
S.no. State/UT Amount Released 1. Madhya Pradesh Rs 46.93 lakh 2. West Bengal Rs 44.76 lakh 3. Odisha Rs 44.08 lakh 4. Gujarat Rs 34.76 lakh 5. Andhra Pradesh Rs 29.21 lakh 6. Bihar Rs 29.20 lakh 7. Karnataka Rs 21.34 lakh 8. Chhattisgarh Rs 18.49 lakh 9. Tamil Nadu Rs 16.57 lakh 10. Uttar Pradesh Rs 16.24 lakh 11. Maharashtra Rs 16.15 lakh 12. Telangana Rs 9.24 lakh 13. Haryana Rs 8.76 lakh 14. Assam Rs 8.49 lakh 15. Jharkhand Rs 8.14 lakh 16. Punjab Rs 7.41 lakh 17. Rajasthan Rs 5.17 lakh 18. Others Rs 13.70 lakh
The recipient SBBs and UTBCs are required to utilise these funds for activities such as preparation and updating People's Biodiversity Registers, in-situ and ex-situ conservation of biodiversity, strengthening of Biodiversity Heritage Sites, capacity building of Biodiversity Management Committees, and socio-economic development of local communities. This ensures that benefits arising from the commercial use of India's biological resources are reinvested in biodiversity conservation and community welfare.
These releases reaffirm India's commitment to implementing the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, particularly Target 13 on the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the use of genetic resources and Target 4 on conserving genetic diversity. The initiative also contributes to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), SDG 15 (Life on Land) and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals).
With cumulative ABS disbursements by the NBA now exceeding Rs. 166 crore, each release further strengthens the link between biodiversity conservation, scientific research and the livelihoods of the communities that conserve India's rich biological resources.

ministry.name: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

enrichment.summary: The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed nearly Rs. 3.79 crore under the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) mechanism to 33 State Biodiversity Boards/UT Biodiversity Councils, ICAR-NBPGR, and the Hisar Bovine Sperm Station and Research Centre. The funds were realised from companies like Bayer Science and Innovation, HM Clause India, and Advanta Enterprises for accessing vegetable, oilseed and Sahiwal cattle germplasm, plus a contribution from Sri Lanka's government for Sahiwal semen access. Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal and Odisha received the largest shares, and cumulative NBA ABS disbursements have now crossed Rs. 166 crore.
enrichment.context:
The Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) mechanism is a core pillar of India's Biological Diversity Act, 2002, enacted to give effect to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and later aligned with the Nagoya Protocol on Access to Genetic Resources and Fair and Equitable Sharing of Benefits (2010). It ensures that when companies or foreign entities commercially exploit India's genetic resources — whether crop germplasm, animal genetic material or traditional knowledge — a share of the resulting benefits flows back to the states and communities that conserve those resources. The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA), a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, regulates such access and administers benefit-sharing through State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs), which channel funds into local conservation activities like People's Biodiversity Registers, Biodiversity Heritage Sites, and Biodiversity Management Committees.

This disbursement is significant because it operationalises the principle of benefit-sharing even where the original geographic source of a resource cannot be pinpointed (since companies often access germplasm through markets or intermediaries) — in such cases, the NBA uses expert-committee-approved formulas based on cultivation-area data to proportionately distribute funds among relevant states. The release also ties India's domestic legal framework to global commitments: the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework's Target 13 (fair and equitable benefit-sharing) and Target 4 (conserving genetic diversity), as well as multiple SDGs. With cumulative ABS disbursements now exceeding Rs. 166 crore, this reflects a growing, tangible mechanism linking biodiversity conservation, agricultural research, and community livelihoods — relevant amid ongoing debates about biopiracy, farmers' rights over genetic resources, and India's implementation of international environmental treaties.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Access and Benefit Sharing' (ABS) mechanism discussed in the context of India's biodiversity governance is implemented under which legislation?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that India's ABS framework is implemented under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, aligned with the Nagoya Protocol.

prelims_questions.question: The Nagoya Protocol, referenced in relation to India's Access and Benefit Sharing framework, is a supplementary agreement to which international convention?
options: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species
prelims_questions.explanation: The Nagoya Protocol is an international agreement supplementing the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), governing access to genetic resources and fair benefit-sharing.
